installer_meta.maintainer_note: FreeBSD provisioning is native: gpart for the layout, base.txz for the userland and kernel.txz for the kernel (base.txz has none), and the loader reads ZFS directly, so there is no UKI and no Clover. The release is not pinned: an empty suite makes the installer run bootstrap.latest_suite, the newest release on the mirror that ships kernel.txz. A FreeBSD target requires a FreeBSD installer environment - Linux hosts cannot run gpart/pkg, which is why the installer filters targets by os_family.

partitioning.list_disks: for d in $(sysctl -n kern.disks); do printf '%s %s %s\n' "$d" "$(diskinfo $d | cut -f3)" "$(diskinfo -v $d | sed -n 's/.*descr.*: *//p')"; done
partitioning.disk_pools: for d in {disk} {disk}p* {disk}s*; do [ -c "$d" ] || continue; n=$(zdb -l "$d" 2>/dev/null | sed -n "s/^ *name: .\(.*\).$/\1/p" | head -n 1); if [ -n "$n" ]; then echo "$d zfs_member $n"; else echo "$d"; fi; done

rootpool.create: zpool create {force} -o ashift={ashift} -O aclinherit=passthrough -O aclmode=passthrough -O canmount=off -O compression={compression} -O atime=off -O mountpoint=/ -R {altroot} {pool_name} {device}

bootstrap.latest_suite: for r in $(fetch -qo - https://download.freebsd.org/ftp/releases/{arch}/ | grep -o '[0-9][0-9]*\.[0-9][0-9]*-RELEASE' | sort -u -t. -k1,1nr -k2,2nr); do fetch -qs https://download.freebsd.org/ftp/releases/{arch}/$r/kernel.txz >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo $r && break; done

rc_conf.content:
hostname="{fqdn}"
zfs_enable="YES"
sshd_enable="YES"
ifconfig_DEFAULT="DHCP"
nfsv4_server_enable="YES"
ntpd_enable="YES"
ntpd_sync_on_start="YES"

fstab.content:
# /etc/fstab - ZFS datasets are mounted by ZFS, not fstab
/dev/gpt/efiboot	/boot/efi	msdosfs	rw	2	2

samba_conf.content:
# Written by the FreedomNAS installer. Shares are created as usershares
# (net usershare) by the WebUI, so only the global settings live here.
[global]
   workgroup = WORKGROUP
   server string = FreedomNAS
   server role = standalone server
   security = user
   log file = /var/log/samba4/%m.log
   max log size = 1000
   usershare path = /var/db/samba4/usershares
   usershare max shares = 100
   usershare allow guests = no

nfs_exports.content:
# NFSv4 clients see the exports below through this root; the exports
# themselves are added by FreedomNAS, one line each (exports(5)).
V4: /

scheduled_jobs.content:
# FreedomNAS scheduled work. Cron decides when; config.yaml decides what,
# so a system with no policies costs a handful of no-ops a day.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
PYTHONPATH={install_root}/core
0  * * * *  root  python3 -m freedomnas snapshot-run --interval hourly  >> /var/log/freedomnas-scheduled.log 2>&1
5  0 * * *  root  python3 -m freedomnas snapshot-run --interval daily   >> /var/log/freedomnas-scheduled.log 2>&1
10 0 * * 0  root  python3 -m freedomnas snapshot-run --interval weekly  >> /var/log/freedomnas-scheduled.log 2>&1
15 0 1 * *  root  python3 -m freedomnas snapshot-run --interval monthly >> /var/log/freedomnas-scheduled.log 2>&1
# The configuration's shadow copy on every other pool: what a reinstall
# onto a blank disk finds waiting for it on the data pool.
30 3 * * *  root  python3 -m freedomnas shadow-sync                     >> /var/log/freedomnas-scheduled.log 2>&1

webui_cron._note: FreeBSD's cron is vixie-cron heritage and honours @reboot, but base ships no /etc/cron.d drop-in directory, so the entry is appended to the system crontab.

sudoers.content:
# FreedomNAS: the WebUI runs updates as the signed-in user,
# and topgrade calls sudo itself for the steps that need root.
%{sudo_group} ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL
